snippet: The bill is titled "Victim Services Amendments" for the 2023 General Session. House Sponsor: Kera Birkeland. Senate Sponsor: Michael K. McKell. The bill specifies that an abortion based upon rape, rape of a child, or incest requires that the unborn child has not reached 18 weeks gestational age. Before performing such an abortion, the physician must verify that the incident has been reported to law enforcement and maintain accurate records. The bill establishes three circumstances permitting abortion: (1) life/health endangerment to the pregnant woman, (2) severe fetal abnormalities with two maternal-fetal medicine physicians' concurrence, (3) pregnancies from rape, rape of a child, or incest (limited to pre-18 week gestational age).

The Senate voted 21-8 to give final approval to the override, one vote over the margin needed for the supermajority. At least four Republican lawmakers from both bodies needed to switch their initial votes in opposition to HB11 to support the override. When the vote came, enough did. Sens. The Utah Senate voted unanimously Tuesday to approve a new version of SB150 after its sponsor, Sen. Todd Weiler, R-Woods Cross, negotiated with LGBTQ+ advocates and others to make clear it shouldn't jeopardize laws the Utah Legislature has passed over the years to protect LGBTQ+ and other civil rights. The latest version of the bill contains "carefully negotiated" language meant to "complement rather than disrupt" Utah's existing legal protections for LGBTQ+ Utahns. SB150 would ban Utah government entities from being able to "substantially burden" a person's constitutional right to freedom of religion unless doing so is "essential to furthering a compelling governmental interest." The bill is modeled after Arizona's similar legislation.

The Utah Senate education committee voted 7-2 to advance House Bill 215. Senator Mike McKell (R-Spanish Fork) voted in favor of the bill. Shauna Warnick, a Nebo School District Board member, expressed disappointment: "He is normally a great supporter of public education and I'm disappointed with his choice, but I very much respect my senator." The "Utah Fits All Scholarship Program" would provide $8,000 vouchers for students to attend private schools or pay for homeschool expenses, with teacher salary raises dependent on the implementation and funding of this program.

HB 215 is titled "Funding for Teacher Salaries and Optional Education Opportunities." House Sponsor: Rep. Candice B. Pierucci. Floor Sponsor: Sen. Kirk A. Cullimore. The Senate passed the bill on third reading with a vote of 20-8-1 (20 yes, 8 no, 1 absent/abstain) on January 26, 2023. The bill was signed by the Governor on January 28, 2023, and became effective May 3, 2023 as the Utah Fits All Scholarship program providing education savings accounts to all Utah families.

Senate sponsor Mike McKell, R-Spanish Fork, emphasized that maintaining accessible mail voting remained important, particularly for rural Utahns, while also incorporating security improvements. "Let me be clear, one of the priorities for the Senate is to preserve vote by mail. We want it to be convenient. But we will address those concerns in the bill. We will enhance security." McKell cited logistical challenges as the Senate's primary objection to the original bill's requirements for staffed drop boxes: "We heard back from counties that it would have added significant costs but not improved the security."

HB 300 was scaled back through negotiations by Sen. Mike McKell to require Utah voters to write the last four digits of their ID on their ballot's return envelope beginning in 2026 and slowly phase out Utah's current automatic vote-by-mail system, setting a deadline of January 1, 2029. McKell said of the new version of the bill: "We want voting as easy as possible without cheating, but we also wanted to make sure that we enhanced security."

The 2021 Legislative Redistricting Committee included Senate Members: Sen. Scott D. Sandall (R) Chair; Sen. Kirk A. Cullimore (R); Sen. Gene Davis; Sen. Lincoln Fillmore (R); Sen. Don L. Ipson (R); Sen. Karen Mayne; Sen. Michael K. McKell (R). The committee was charged with drawing new maps following the 2020 census. The Republican-majority committee voted along party lines to adopt legislatively drawn maps over the independent commission's recommendations, rejecting all maps proposed by the advisory Independent Redistricting Commission established by voter-approved Proposition 4 in 2018.

Utah's Legislative Redistricting Committee voted to adopt its own voter districts, voting along party lines with Republicans outnumbering Democrats, to approve congressional maps and forward them to the full Utah Legislature. The new map drawn by the state Legislature largely ignored a set of plans proposed by the state's advisory Independent Redistricting Commission. Utah's redistricting battle exemplified a clash between the legislature's claimed authority and the voter-approved Prop 4 independent commission. The Senate voted 21-7 to approve the map, which gave the congressional map final approval it needed to clear the Republican-controlled Utah Legislature.

McKell initially objected to earlier versions of HB 226 over concerns about provisions affecting legal immigrants, but supported the revised version of the deportation bill once those concerns were addressed.

Despite initially voting to table HB 226, McKell and other GOP leaders insisted they were still on board with Trump's mass deportations and would support a narrowed version of the legislation that focused on criminal immigrants.

The Utah Legislature approved a $167 million income tax cut largely benefitting high earners. SB 69 lowers the income tax from 4.65% to 4.55%. The bill sailed easily through the GOP-controlled Utah Legislature, passing the Senate 23-6 on January 31, 2024, and the House 63-11 on February 28, 2024. Since 2021, Utah's tax rate has dropped from 4.95% to 4.85% in 2022, 4.65% in 2023, 4.55% in 2024, and 4.5% in 2025.

Sen. McKell stated: "In Utah, we care deeply about our teen's mental health. Since 2009, depression, anxiety and suicidal ideation has drastically increased among minors in Utah and across the United States. After reviewing the data and talking with teens and parents, I decided to run S.B. 152 Social Media Regulation Amendments. Utah is leading the way to fight back against the harms of social media and providing parents with more resources and controls. As a lawmaker and parent, I believe we are helping prevent our children from succumbing to social media's negative and sometimes life-threatening effects." He cited CDC findings showing 57% of teen girls experience persistent sadness and nearly one-third contemplated suicide as motivation for the legislation.

HB 261 is titled 'Equal Opportunity Initiatives' for the 2024 General Session. House Sponsor: Rep. Katy Hall. Senate Floor Sponsor: Sen. Keith Grover. The Senate passed the bill on third reading with a vote of 23-6-0 on January 25, 2024. The bill was signed by the Governor. Roll call records show McKell, M. voted YES among the 23 senators supporting the measure. The six no votes came from Democratic senators.

Utah's DEI bill easily passed the Senate with a party-line vote of 23-6, and passed the House 59-14. The bill, titled 'Equal Opportunity Initiatives,' is one of the highest profile 'culture war' measures from the 2024 legislative session and would overhaul diversity, equity and inclusion programs at public institutions in the state and replace them with resource centers open to all 'high risk' individuals. The bill aims to outlaw DEI trainings, requirements, programs and offices at public universities, schools 'or any other institution of the state' that engages in what the legislation calls 'prohibited discriminatory practices.'
